$comment: The minimal map that still runs every Walmart-era flow: one EasyLoop (two pick places on one belt), inventory induction, box induction, extraction, an order-tote depot, an order buffer worked by a gripper, a highway and open floor. It is the EARLY gate for a development cycle -- fast enough to run on every change -- with walmart_dfw6.json kept for the final gate. Site-agnostic: no geometry or name here comes from any customer. GENERATED by scripts/gen_minimal_easyloop.py; regenerate rather than hand-edit. The EasyLoop is authored cell by cell: one machine entity carrying a frame and the `easyloop` envelope, 28 declared cells posed in that frame, three lanes that name the place each serves, and an explicit stitch per arc. `pick` on a presentation cell is what makes it a pick place -- the happening that used to be a `station` component's `kind` -- and this reader knows it by name, so it is REQUIRED: a consumer blind to it would load a machine with no pick places at all. Two things this copy spells differently, both forced by the older reader it is written for: a queue step names its cell instead of stating the position of one, and a band that must not tile under the machine is written as the regions its envelope leaves standing instead of as one region with a carve-out. GENERATED by scripts/gen_minimal_easyloop.py --vocabulary master.

template.$comment: The same steel with `holds` replaced, which is the whole difference between stock racking and order racking.

components.$comment: Stock, and the only steel putaway may deposit into.

Order bays in an INVENTORY aisle, which is what makes them the depot: where an unused order tote waits until close-out loads an order into it. A separate stamp because a run is one stamp of one template and its bays cannot disagree on what they hold.
Order bays in an ORDER aisle, which is what makes them the buffer: capacity for a closed order that has not been picked yet, so nothing is seeded into them.
The strip the climbing class works from. It declares NO tiling: tiling follows locomotion, and a lane nothing drives is not floor.
The buffer's own aisle, so its racking is a zone of its own and a gripper is the only machine assigned to it.

robot_class.$comment: A gripper works the buffer; a vacuum head works stock. One aisle is worked by one kind of machine.

cohort.$comment: EIGHT, and the two above six are what the buffer detour costs. At six the run wedges: putaway staging holds four HTMs carrying empty totes while a closed order waits for one to fetch it back out of the buffer, and neither side yields. Eight clears it; the wedge itself is recorded in tests/minimal_easyloop.rs.

carrier_type.$comment: One physical tote type; inventory-vs-order is a per-instance designation, not a different type.

carrier_pool.$comment: One tote per position of the depot, which is where they stand. Close-out has nothing to load an order into if this is zero.
